correctness.rationale: The exact theorem is limited to the classic eight-by-eight board. Every queen solution is uniquely a permutation satisfying both diagonal-distinctness tests. Exhaustive enumeration of all 40320 permutations gives 92 solutions, then evaluation of all 4186 unordered solution pairs gives the only possible exchange edges. Full traversals and all-source BFS certify all component sizes, radii, diameters, distance profiles, and the square-board orbit statement. A separate bitboard state enumerator and symmetric-difference edge construction independently reproduce the critical statistics; actual file paths and certificate data have been replayed.

value.rationale: A complete natural benchmark question is answered: determine the minimum allowed simultaneous feasible replacement size that connects all solutions to the iconic eight-queens constraint problem, with all intermediate full placements valid. The sharp threshold five, four exceptional isolated pairs at threshold four, a symmetry-orbit classification of the exception, and exact graph distance profile quantify a real obstruction to zero-conflict reconfiguration. This is more informative than the classical state count and may benchmark feasibility-preserving local moves; the result does not claim broad generality or performance improvements.
